activeForm: Fixing open on a closed descriptor
description:
FILED s404 (Opus 5), found while fixing #346's fd leak.

    perl -e 'my $ok = open(my $t, "<&=9"); print $ok ? "SUCCEEDED" : "failed ($!)"'
        perl: failed (Bad file descriptor)
        PCL : SUCCEEDED

PCL's open does not validate the descriptor in the `<&=N` (fdopen) spelling —
it hands back a filehandle for a descriptor that is not open.  A program that
uses the failure as its signal reads PCL's answer as "inherited" no matter
what, and t/run/cloexec.t is exactly that program: it opens fd 3, spawns a
child, and asks whether the child can still open it.

LAYER: the runtime (cl/pcl-runtime.lisp, p-open's fd path), not the parser.
Rule 12 in its die-vs-announce form: an open that cannot be satisfied must FAIL
like perl and set $!, not succeed with a handle nothing can read.

BAR: the probe above identical to perl for (a) a never-opened fd, (b) an open
one, (c) one opened and then closed; a Pl/t row; and re-run run/cloexec.t under
PERL=tools/pclperl-for-tests (task #346) to see what it scores once open()
tells the truth.

NOTE the ordering: #346's fd-leak fix removed the reason fd 3 was open in a PCL
child, so this bug is now the REMAINING reason cloexec.t cannot measure what it
means to measure.


CLOSED s405 (8609e38): one fcntl(F_GETFD) in %p-open-dup.  Guard rows in Pl/t/fileio-02.t.
subject: SILENT WRONG: open(FH, "<&=N") SUCCEEDS on a closed descriptor (perl fails EBADF)
